title: Intelligent electric vehicles and embodied intelligence — isometric research illustration
purpose: A conceptual illustration of the group's research themes, with no in-image text or figure numbering.
processing: Original generated PNG copied into the workspace; JPEG export for web delivery. No cropping.
prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: a finished editorial technical illustration for the hero of an academic research-group website, “zhang’s group”. Generate ONLY the illustration, not a website, poster, screenshot or layout mockup. Landscape 4:3 composition.
Primary request: an exceptionally refined, restrained blue-gray isometric illustration combining intelligent electric vehicles and embodied intelligence. Think of a carefully art-directed scientific magazine opener drawn by a skilled technical illustrator. Crisp, deliberate linework with a little depth and elegant negative space. This is an illustration, NOT a photograph and NOT a photorealistic 3D render.
Subjects and hierarchy: in the lower left, an elegant unbranded electric research car with realistic passenger-car proportions, a gently sculpted hood, convincing greenhouse/windows, discreet roof lidar and properly aligned rubber wheels. The car is not a box, toy or cartoon. In the upper right, a precisely constructed slender six-axis robot arm on a simple low rectangular base, with articulated elbow, visible circular joints, and a credible two-finger gripper holding ONE small rectangular block directly over a small test surface. Make the arm sophisticated and anatomically/mechanically plausible, not a giant claw crane. Car and robot should each be instantly recognizable, with neither dwarfing the other.
Composition: one coherent axonometric world, 30-degree isometric view, shared perspective and ground plane. The car faces toward the lower-left foreground; the robot faces inward toward the car, leaving an elegant diagonal open corridor through the middle. A very faint curved dashed path on the ground joins their zones and suggests perception and planning. Just two restrained translucent blue sensing arcs near the car, subtle enough not to distract. Optional one low geometric architectural outline in the far background to establish depth. The ground plane gently fades into the surrounding paper, without a thick diamond tile or a heavy frame. Main objects occupy 70–75% of the canvas; generous margins, no cropped wheels, no oversized empty bottom third.
Style: sophisticated contemporary technical editorial illustration, precise clean silhouettes, controlled fine outlines, selected flat tonal faces, understated ambient shadows. Mostly flat vector-like visual language with a small amount of soft dimensional shading. Outer contours slightly stronger than interior seams. Spend detail on the car's shape, robot joints and simple gripper, not tiny decorative clutter. No shaky sketch lines.
Palette: very pale cool gray/off-white paper background #f2f5f8, midnight navy #22476b, slate blue #6c91b1, soft blue-gray #c7d7e5, near-white highlights; a restrained 4–5-tone palette. A few deep blue surfaces create crisp focal points. Keep background almost white. No saturated or neon colors. The asset sits as a light illustrated panel on a dark navy website.
Text: absolutely none. No letters, no numbers, no labels, no FIG, no legends, no captions, no logos, no watermarks, no corner decorations. All webpage text will be added in HTML separately.
Avoid: childlike blocky car, toy-like proportions, plastic clay 3D, inflated rounded shapes, glossy chrome, stock isometric icon kit, busy full-canvas graph paper, circuit-board wallpaper, extra disconnected mechanical arms, dangling cables, floating machinery, impossible grippers, random geometry, holographic dashboards, sci-fi neon, dramatic bloom, photo textures, photoreal lab interior, poster borders or footer rules. Aim for calm, precise, beautifully balanced academic illustration.
